lines.text: This is a content studio. It lives in your terminal, and you use it by talking to it.
First run, it asks about your brand. Your colours, your type, the way you sound.
It writes the answers into one file, and from then on, everything you make wears it.
Then you just say what you want.
A carousel about the new pricing. It writes the copy, builds the slides, renders the images, and shows you the picture.
Slide two feels flat? Say so. It re-renders in seconds.
Decks work the same way. Seven slides, one PDF, ready to send.
Writing a long piece? You get the article, the hero image, the share card and the caption, all in one go.
Videos too, and this is the fun part.
Every frame is just HTML, screenshotted by a browser. The sound is synthesized from a little JSON file.
And the motion is one paused timeline. Nothing plays. The renderer asks it for a frame, so the picture can never drift from the voice.
There is no video editor anywhere in this. Not even for what you just watched.
Tell it a post went out, and the calendar ticks itself and re-renders the board.
And it is not tied to one AI. It is just files and a folder of instructions, so point whichever model you already pay for at it.
One hour on a Monday gets you a week of content.
It is open source. Yours in five minutes.
